title: 2027-02-28-pegasus-insurance-commitment-renewal-and-global-edge-plan
summary: Customer (Pegasus) is nearing contract renewal. They want to confirm a 12-month reserved capacity commit with burst credits, add APAC edge and EU private nodes, and pilot a VPC/private deployment for sensitive underwriting data. Redwood clarified dedicated GPU pools, canary/rollback flows, SSO/KMS integrations, and proposed a phased onboarding and benchmark plan. Agreed next steps include a pricing amendment, a security pack (SOC2 + architecture diagram), and a 2-week pilot for private deployment with acceptance checks around P95 latency and sample throughput.
meeting_header: Date: 2027-02-28 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen, Luis Ortega, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Elena Rodriguez, Tom Baxter, Ravi Kumar, Sofia Lee (Pegasus) | Recording: yes
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Elena Rodriguez: Elena here, hi.
[00:00:08] Tom Baxter: Tom on infra.
[00:00:10] Ravi Kumar: Ravi from security.
[00:00:12] Sofia Lee: Sofia product.
[00:00:14] Maya Chen: Great. Luis and Priya from our side as well. We'll keep this to about 45 minutes. Main goal: renewal terms, APAC/EU onboarding, and private pilot asks.
[00:00:28] Luis Ortega: quick heads up, I'll cover the throughput/latency part and the pilot runbook.
[00:00:34] Elena Rodriguez: sounds good. So high level we're prepared to renew, we just need clarity on guarantees for APAC latency and the VPC/private option for underwriting data, which is PHI-adjacent. Also price ok but want committed discount if we commit 12 months.
[00:00:54] Maya Chen: totally. We can offer a 12-month reserved capacity agreement with burst credits layered on top. Typical structure: base reserved QPS/capacity and a burst pool billed at a lower committed rate than on-demand.
[00:01:06] Sofia Lee: can you put numbers to that? rough order?
[00:01:10] Maya Chen: rough - for your current usage profile (based on last quarter telemetry), we'd recommend a commit of 32 dedicated GPUs-equivalent for baseline and a 20% burst pool. We'll get finance to surface exact price tiers but that'll be around a 22-28% effective discount vs pure on-demand.
[00:01:32] Tom Baxter: 32 GPUs eq — does that map to a specific instance type? we run in GCP us-west and have some apac infra.
[00:01:40] Luis Ortega: it's an abstraction; under the hood that maps to our dedicated host pools. We select optimized kernels and instance types for the models you run. For APAC edge we'll spin up dedicated racks in the region we agreed on — Tokyo and Singapore are typical.
[00:01:54] Ravi Kumar: on the private pilot: we need to know how keys are handled, KMS/HSM options, and whether logs that contain prompts are retained. SOC 2 is a requirement for us.
[00:02:05] Priya Nair: we will share our SOC 2 report and the security pack. For the private pilot we support customer-managed KMS; if you want HSM we can integrate with your provider. Regarding logs, we have configurable retention and masking — by default the private mode can be configured to not retain prompts, only telemetry and metrics.
[00:02:26] Elena Rodriguez: that's helpful. For compliance we also need SAML SSO + RBAC for the console and strict audit logs.
[00:02:33] Maya Chen: yes SAML + SCIM provisioning is supported; RBAC roles map to admin/operator/viewer. Audit logs are exportable to your SIEM and we can show retention settings.
[00:02:46] Sofia Lee: timeline question: we need APAC edge live by end of Q2. EU private nodes by mid-Q3. Are those realistic?
[00:02:55] Luis Ortega: APAC end of Q2 is feasible if we start provisioning next week — site procurement and infra burn take 4–6 weeks, then onboarding and benchmarks 2–3 weeks. EU private mid-Q3: that's tight but doable, depends on procurement/legal turnaround.
[00:03:12] Tom Baxter: what about runbook for canary and rollback? we can't have a bad rollout hitting production underwriting.
[00:03:19] Luis Ortega: we recommend canary traffic routing at 5% for 48 hours, automated health checks tied to latency and error rate, then staged ramp to 50% over a week. Automatic fallback to previous model variant or to hosted region if health checks fail.
[00:03:34] Ravi Kumar: how deterministic is your latency? our SLAs need P95 < 200ms for short prompts (under 512 tokens).
[00:03:41] Luis Ortega: for short prompts on dedicated pools in region, P95 under 200ms is achievable for smaller models; for larger context or long sequences P95 will vary. We can run a short benchmark suite during the pilot to validate.
[00:03:53] Elena Rodriguez: can you guarantee that in contract language?
[00:03:56] Maya Chen: SLA language we can include latency targets for specific routes and model versions, with credits for breaches. We'll need to define the exact models and request size envelope in the SLO appendix.
[00:04:06] Sofia Lee: pricing — if we go 12 months commitment, what's the uplift for adding APAC/EU? is that extra committed capacity or part of the same pool?
[00:04:15] Maya Chen: we can carve regional commitments as separate seat pools or a global pool with regional minimums. Usually customers prefer regional carve-outs for predictability; price per unit is similar but there is a one-time onboarding fee for each region for provisioning.
[00:04:31] Tom Baxter: onboarding fee — do you have typical numbers?
[00:04:34] Maya Chen: typically $12k–$25k per region depending on private vs hosted and network complexity. We'll outline exact in the amendment.
[00:04:42] Ravi Kumar: network flow: for private VPC, does traffic egress Redwood's control plane? we can't have sensitive payloads touching public infra.
[00:04:50] Luis Ortega: private deployment option keeps inference nodes in your VPC; the control plane can be run in a customer-managed subnet or we can use a private peering model. Data plane stays in your environment; only telemetry metadata can be routed to Redwood's control plane optionally. We can mask prompts locally.
[00:05:07] Elena Rodriguez: ok good. Will need architecture diagram.
[00:05:09] Priya Nair: we'll attach the architecture diagram in the security pack.
[00:05:14] Sofia Lee: acceptance criteria for the pilot — what are you proposing?
[00:05:18] Luis Ortega: two-week pilot: week one is provisioning and smoke tests; week two is controlled load tests with your workload – we run 72-hour soak at target TPS and measure P50/P95/P99, error rates, and token cost. Acceptance if P95 < 200ms and error rate < 0.5% for the defined envelope.
[00:05:34] Elena Rodriguez: and billing during pilot?
[00:05:37] Maya Chen: pilot billed at a discounted pilot rate or credit applied to future committed balance. We can cover a portion if you move forward with commit.
[00:05:44] Tom Baxter: re model variants: we use a mix of open models and a licensed variant. will you support mixing variants across regions?
[00:05:50] Luis Ortega: yes. Smart routing can route by policy. We can pin model versions per route. Fallbacks to compatible variants when capacity constrained are supported.
[00:05:59] Ravi Kumar: what about encryption at rest / in flight?
[00:06:02] Priya Nair: TLS in transit, encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS for private deployments. We can use HSM-backed keys if needed.
[00:06:09] Sofia Lee: any regulatory constraints for EU private nodes? data residency?
[00:06:13] Maya Chen: EU private nodes fulfill residency — logs retained per your policy and processed inside the EU cluster. We'll provide DPA language.
[00:06:21] Elena Rodriguez: ok sounds promising. A couple of items — we want a committed uplift for inference cost predictability, plus an option to burst for seasonal spikes. Also want a short SLA for model rollouts; canary windows need to be contractually enforced.
[00:06:35] Maya Chen: we'll capture canary policy and rollback triggers in the rollouts appendix. Bursting is already in the proposed approach. We'll get legal to draft an amendment with these clauses.
[00:06:46] Sofia Lee: question — we run some latency-sensitive features in APAC; will the model quantization or 4-bit optimizations change quality? we can't accept degradation for underwriting.
[00:06:57] Luis Ortega: quantization can change numeric fidelity; we recommend running evals on your prompt set. Redwood Optimize will suggest quant profiles per workload; quality regression monitoring will be part of the rollout — we can tie regressions to automated rollback.
[00:07:10] Elena Rodriguez: can you run a quick eval on a small set this week? maybe 50 representative prompts?
[00:07:14] Luis Ortega: yes we can. Send the 50 prompts, we'll run the eval with the candidate quantized profile and share delta metrics.
[00:07:20] Maya Chen: perfect — that's one of the next steps.
[00:07:23] [brief pause, crosstalk]
[00:07:34] Tom Baxter: ops question: autoscaling — is scaling per model instance or per GPU pool? how fast does it scale on demand?
[00:07:41] Luis Ortega: scales at the pool level; continuous batching and autoscale policies can add capacity within minutes for warm pools, cold start to full may take longer depending on cold provisioning. With reserved capacity we can keep warm instances to reduce cold starts.
[00:07:56] Ravi Kumar: we need to ensure no hidden egress costs or data flows to third parties.
[00:08:01] Priya Nair: we'll include an egress and data-flow section in the security pack and the DPA.
[00:08:07] Sofia Lee: procurement timeline — we want to execute amendment by March 31 to lock pricing for Q2.
[00:08:14] Maya Chen: timeline workable. We'll get a pricing amendment draft in your inbox by next Tuesday (Mar 2).
[00:08:20] Elena Rodriguez: and security docs?
[00:08:22] Priya Nair: security pack and SOC2 will be shared within 3 business days. Architecture diagram included.
[00:08:28] Maya Chen: ok let's recap.
[00:08:30] Maya Chen: Recap: (1) 12-month reserved commit proposal — baseline 32 GPUs eq with 20% burst pool, (2) APAC edge provisioning targeted end of Q2, EU private mid-Q3, (3) 2-week private VPC pilot with acceptance criteria (P95 < 200ms, error rate < 0.5%), (4) security pack and SOC2 to be delivered, (5) pricing amendment draft by Mar 2, (6) evaluation run of 50 prompts by Redwood SE.
[00:09:02] Elena Rodriguez: that covers it. A couple more follow-ups: can you include an explicit statement about rollback to hosted region if APAC edge has an incident?
[00:09:12] Luis Ortega: yes we can include automated fallback to nearest healthy region as a contract appendix.
[00:09:18] Tom Baxter: we'll also need a runbook for incident response and an on-call contact during the initial 90 days.
[00:09:24] Maya Chen: we'll provide the runbook and a dedicated on-call rotation for the first 90 days post-onboarding.
[00:09:30] Elena Rodriguez: great.
[00:09:33] [00:09:33 - 00:46:00 – meeting wraps with informal conversation and scheduling follow-up]
[00:09:35] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. I'll send the notes and next steps.
[00:09:38] Priya Nair: thanks, bye.
[00:09:40] Elena Rodriguez: thanks, bye.
action_items: Maya Chen - Send pricing amendment draft - Due: 2027-03-02
Priya Nair - Share SOC 2 report + security pack + architecture diagram - Due: 2027-03-03
Luis Ortega - Run eval on 50 prompts and share results - Due: 2027-03-05
Redwood Engineering - Draft canary and rollback appendix for contract - Due: 2027-03-10
next_steps: Pegasus to compile 50 representative prompts and send to Luis by Mar 1
Security deliverables shared by Priya within 3 business days
Schedule private pilot provisioning kickoff next week (tentative Mar 4)
